issues.sym: With a heavy load on board, the truck can feel unstable or tippy during sharp or sudden steering.
issues.why: On two-wheel-drive trucks, a combination of heavy loading and hard steering could make the vehicle lose stability. Toyota recalled these trucks for a free fix.
issues.next: Check the VIN for an open recall and have it done before carrying heavy loads. Avoid overloading and sudden swerves until it is fixed.

issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, loose or wandering steering, or uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: The front lower ball joints can wear faster than they should. A badly worn joint can pull apart from the steering knuckle, letting the wheel fold under the truck. Toyota recalled these years to replace them.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the ball joints inspected right away. Do not keep driving with a clunking front end.

issues.sym: Flaking or bubbling rust on the frame rails and crossmembers, holes in the frame, or new creaks and clunks from underneath.
issues.why: The frame's protective coating breaks down under road salt, and on many trucks the rust eventually eats through structural parts of the frame.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift, especially before buying one of these trucks. A frame with holes is a safety risk and should be repaired or replaced before regular driving.

issues.sym: Raw fuel smell from the engine bay or wetness around the fuel rail.
issues.why: The fuel pulsation damper on some early 2003 trucks may not have been put together correctly and can leak fuel near hot engine parts.
issues.next: Any fuel smell means stop and get it checked. Confirm by VIN that the recall was done.

issues.sym: Long cracks across the top of the dash, sometimes near the passenger airbag area.
issues.why: The soft dash pad breaks down from heat and sun over the years. Toyota issued a bulletin and extended coverage at the time, but that coverage is long over.
issues.next: Not a driving hazard on its own. A dash cover or a replacement dash pad fixes the look.

issues.t: Floor mat can trap the gas pedal (recall 11V113)
issues.sym: The gas pedal sticks down or returns slowly, and the truck keeps accelerating.
issues.why: An unsecured or wrong floor mat can slide forward and hold the accelerator pedal down. Toyota added these trucks to its floor mat recall.
issues.next: Use only a secured mat made for this truck and never stack mats. Check the VIN for the recall. If the pedal sticks, shift to neutral and brake firmly.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may fire without a crash (recall 16V065)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. The side curtain airbags may go off while driving with no collision.
issues.why: A problem in the curtain airbag system could make the bags deploy when they are not needed, which can startle or injure people inside.
issues.next: Check the VIN at Toyota or NHTSA and get the free recall repair done soon.

issues.t: Secondary air injection pump or valve failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, and sometimes the truck runs in a reduced-power mode right after a cold start.
issues.why: The air pump and its switching valve that help clean exhaust on cold starts can fail, often after moisture gets inside. Toyota covered the fix in a bulletin.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the pump and valve tested. Ask a dealer whether the bulletin applies to your truck.

issues.sym: Oily fluid near the front sway bar or shocks, a suspension warning, a harsher ride, or the truck leaning to one side.
issues.why: Trucks with KDSS or the X-REAS shock system use hydraulic lines and cylinders that can corrode or wear and start leaking with age.
issues.next: Have the system inspected and the leak fixed. Rinse the underside after driving on salted roads to slow corrosion.

issues.sym: Firm or jerky shifts at low speed, especially when slowing down and pulling away again.
issues.why: Early fifth-generation trucks had transmission shift complaints that Toyota addressed with a dealer update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether a software update or bulletin applies. If shifts get worse or the truck slips, have it checked sooner.

issues.sym: One or more doors will not lock or unlock with the key fob or switch, or the doors do not auto-lock.
issues.why: The small motors inside the door latches wear out and stop working on many trucks of this era.
issues.next: Have the failed actuator replaced. Lock that door by hand in the meantime.

issues.sym: The touchscreen locks up, restarts on its own, or is very slow to respond.
issues.why: The head unit software of this period is prone to glitches. Firmware updates fix many cases, and some units need replacing.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for any available software update. Replace the unit only if updates do not help.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail and stall the engine (recall 20V012)
issues.sym: Rough running, check engine light, failure to start, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump in the tank can fail, cutting fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and get the free pump replacement. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Grille or hood overlay can come loose (recall 17V763)
issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the truck or a trim piece on the hood or grille that feels loose.
issues.why: A fastener holding the decorative overlay can break, letting the piece come off while driving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the fasteners replaced. Do not drive at highway speed with loose front trim.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail and stall the engine (recall 20V682)
issues.sym: Rough running, check engine light, failure to start, or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: The same low-pressure fuel pump problem found on earlier years was later recalled on these trucks too.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and get the free pump replacement. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.sym: Clunks or knocks from the front, a loose steering feel, or the truck pulling to one side.
issues.why: Some steering and suspension fasteners may not have been tightened enough at the factory and can work loose.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the bolts inspected and tightened soon. Stop driving if steering feels loose.

issues.t: Gauge cluster may not show speed or warnings (recall 25V595)
issues.sym: After starting, the instrument panel may not display the speedometer, brake warning or tire pressure warning.
issues.why: A software problem in the instrument cluster can keep key information and warnings from showing.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and get the free software fix. Do not drive without a working speedometer and warnings.

issues.t: Rough or clunky shifts from the 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: Jerky or delayed shifts, a clunk when the transmission engages, or unexpected downshifts, mostly at low speed or under load.
issues.why: Owners of the new generation report shift quality problems with the 8-speed automatic shared with the Tacoma. No single cause has been confirmed, and a few transmissions have been replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Report it to a Toyota dealer while under warranty and ask about software updates. Have it checked sooner if it slips or shows warning lights.

issues.t: Head gasket failure on the early 4.0L V6
issues.sym: A rough, shaky idle for the first minute after a cold start, a flashing or steady check engine light with a misfire on one cylinder, a sweet coolant smell from the exhaust, and a coolant level that keeps dropping with no puddle under the truck.
issues.why: On early versions of the 4.0L V6 a head gasket can start to seep, usually at one of the rear cylinders, letting coolant into the cylinder while the engine sits. Owners most often report it well past the hundred-thousand-mile mark.
issues.next: Do not keep driving with a cold-start misfire and falling coolant. Overheating or coolant in a cylinder can ruin the engine. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the cylinders before deciding on a repair.
